Citation: Plonka W, Stork C, Sicho M, Kirchmair J. CYPlebrity: Machine learning models for the prediction of inhibitors of cytochrome P450 enzymes. Bioorg Med Chem. 2021;46:116388.
Training_data_as_stated: Abstract (verified): "combining data from several major public and proprietary sources"; up to 18,815 compounds with measured bioactivities. A secondary review (Front Pharmacol comparison of in silico CYP tools, PMC10543639) lists its sources as "PubChem; ChEMBL; FujitSu ADME" with 134,250 molecules.
Evidence_for_training_data_claim: Abstract read directly from PubMed. Full methods NOT accessible - sciencedirect.com returned HTTP 403. Source list taken from a secondary review, not the primary paper. NO PubChem AID number is given in any source we could read.
Code_or_model_distributed: No code or model found; web service only
Verdict: BEST CANDIDATE but NOT independent: PubChem is among its sources. It is the only tool with a documented substantial NON-PubChem component (ChEMBL + proprietary Fujitsu ADME).

Citation: Daina A, Michielin O, Zoete V. SwissADME: a free web tool to evaluate pharmacokinetics, drug-likeness and medicinal chemistry friendliness of small molecules. Sci Rep. 2017;7:42717.
Training_data_as_stated: Full text, verbatim: "For CYP major isoforms, all datasets were those of Veith et al. and downloaded from the PubChem database (http://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, accessed February 2016)."
Evidence_for_training_data_claim: Primary paper full text retrieved via Europe PMC (PMC5335600) and quoted directly. Veith et al. 2009 Nat Biotechnol is reference 50 in that paper and is the AID 1851 cytochrome panel.
Verdict: NOT INDEPENDENT - same source data as ours.

Citation: Pires DEV, Blundell TL, Ascher DB. pkCSM: Predicting Small-Molecule Pharmacokinetic and Toxicity Properties Using Graph-Based Signatures. J Med Chem. 2015;58(9):4066-72.
Training_data_as_stated: Full text, Table 2: every CYP450 inhibitor model (1A2, 2C19, 2C9, 2D6, 3A4) is listed with "data set method ref: admetSAR". pkCSM did not assemble its own CYP data - it reused admetSAR's.
Evidence_for_training_data_claim: Primary paper full text retrieved via Europe PMC (PMC4434528). The strings "Veith" and "1851" appear ZERO times in it. Its independence is therefore entirely determined by admetSAR's, which we could not establish.
Verdict: NOT USABLE AS INDEPENDENT - its CYP data is admetSAR's, whose provenance is not stated.

Citation: Cheng F, Li W, Zhou Y, Shen J, Wu Z, Liu G, Lee PW, Tang Y. admetSAR: a comprehensive source and free tool for assessment of chemical ADMET properties. J Chem Inf Model. 2012;52(11):3099-3105. | admetSAR 2.0: Yang H, et al. Bioinformatics. 2019;35(6):1067-1069.
Training_data_as_stated: NOT STATED - we could not retrieve the primary methods. Secondary sources describe admetSAR 2.0's general training data as "DrugBank, ChEMBL, CPDB, CYP450 and Tox21", but this is a whole-platform description and names no CYP-specific dataset or PubChem AID.
Evidence_for_training_data_claim: NOT VERIFIED. The 2012 primary paper's methods were not retrieved. Web search returned only secondary descriptions and one source that said the CYP data "most likely" came from PubChem AID 1851 - an inference, not a statement. Recorded as NOT STATED per protocol.
Verdict: CANNOT CLASSIFY - training source not stated in anything we could read. Do not claim it is independent.

Citation: Fu L, Shi S, Yi J, et al. ADMETlab 3.0: an updated comprehensive online ADMET prediction platform. Nucleic Acids Res. 2024;52(W1):W422-W431.
Training_data_as_stated: NOT STATED for CYP specifically. The paper describes the platform as having over 400,000 entries across 119 endpoints. A secondary review states ADMETlab's data were "collected from ChEMBL, EPA, and DrugBank" (288,967 entries), but that same review's own table records the database as "Unspecified" - the review contradicts itself.
Evidence_for_training_data_claim: Abstract verified via PubMed. CYP-specific training source not found in anything we could read. The one secondary source is self-contradictory.
Verdict: CANNOT CLASSIFY - CYP training source not stated.

Citation: Ai D, Cai H, Wei J, Zhao D, Chen Y, Wang L. DEEPCYPs: A deep learning platform for enhanced cytochrome P450 activity prediction. Front Pharmacol. 2023;14:1099093.
Training_data_as_stated: Full text, verified: training data taken from the iCYP-MFE dataset of Nguyen-Vo et al. (2021), compiled from six PubChem BioAssay datasets - AIDs 1851, 410, 883, 889, 891 and 884. 65,467 samples after processing.
Evidence_for_training_data_claim: Primary paper full text read via PMC10123292. AID 1851 is named explicitly among its six sources.
Code_or_model_distributed: YES - local Python software + datasets at https://github.com/idrugLab/FP-GNN_CYP (repo live; pretrained weights in model_save/; last push May 2022)
Reachable_28_Oct_2026: WEB SERVER NO - re-checked twice on 28 Oct 2026: expired SSL certificate, and with certificate verification disabled it returns HTTP 502 Bad Gateway, so the reverse proxy is up but the application behind it is not serving. GITHUB REPO YES (HTTP 200).
Verdict: NOT INDEPENDENT (shares AID 1851) but RUNNABLE LOCALLY - the only tool here we can execute reproducibly.

Citation: Banerjee P, Dunkel M, Kemmler E, Preissner R. SuperCYPsPred - a web server for the prediction of cytochrome activity. Nucleic Acids Res. 2020;48(W1):W580-W585.
Training_data_as_stated: Full text states: "A total of 17,143 substances tested using quantitative high-throughput screening" obtained from "the PubChem Bioassay database, AID: 1815". NOTE: we checked AID 1815 against PubChem and it is "qHTS for differential inhibitors of proliferation of Plasmodium falciparum line 7G8" - a malaria assay, NOT a CYP assay. AID 1851 is "Cytochrome panel assay with activity outcomes" and has ~17,143 substances. The published AID appears to be a typo for 1851, but we record this as an INFERENCE, not a verified fact.
Evidence_for_training_data_claim: Primary paper read via PMC7319455. AIDs 1815 and 1851 both checked against the live PubChem REST API on 28 Oct 2026.
Code_or_model_distributed: No - no source code or downloadable model described
Reachable_28_Oct_2026: NO - re-checked twice on 28 Oct 2026. Connection failed on http, https, bare host and port 8000, while charite.de, pubmed and github all returned HTTP 200 in the same check (so not a local network block)
Verdict: CANNOT BE RUN OR VERIFIED BY ANYONE at present: server unreachable and no code distributed. Reproducibility observation worth reporting.
